milestones.title: First raid with Artimis
milestones.blurb: Mixed-guild Molten Core — the earliest confirmed raid containing Artimis.
milestones.blurbHtml: Mixed-guild Molten Core — the earliest confirmed raid containing Artimis.
milestones.html: The screenshot from 22:09 that night shows a nearly full room gathered before Magmadar, guild tags still mixed — a coalition raid slowly becoming a guild team. Artimis, Dejvid, Divinestorm, Kodf and Jellopy are all in frame: five people whose decisions would shape everything that follows, standing in the same corridor a year before any of it happened.

milestones.title: The hunter diary begins
milestones.blurb: Onyxia and an 8/10 Molten Core clear; Artimis starts organizing the hunters.
milestones.blurbHtml: Onyxia and an 8/10 Molten Core clear; Artimis starts organizing the hunters.
milestones.html:
The screenshot trail from this week shows Artimis stepping, almost by accident, into the job that would define his Classic: invited to the officer meeting on the 13th, and within days coordinating the hunter channel, the gear records, the tranquilizing-shot rotation and the signups. He had joined to collect tier pieces. The spreadsheets had other plans.

By 10 November the job had become personal diplomacy. Knedlica had won a better gun, while Ravna and Nereb still carried weaker bows, so Artimis asked whether they could receive the next Ancient Petrified Leaves first. Knedlica agreed and supplied his own weapon-speed theorycraft. Artimis finished Rhok'delar around 11 November. The class was learning loot policy and raid mechanics in the same conversation.

milestones.title: Ragnaros down, the Choker drops
milestones.blurb: The kill screenshot survives; the neck later fuels the guild's first loot dispute.
milestones.blurbHtml: The kill screenshot survives; the neck later fuels the guild's first loot dispute.
milestones.html:
The Choker of the Fire Lord is one of the rarest drops in Molten Core and best-in-slot for every caster and healer in the raid — which made it a test the young guild's loot rules weren't ready for. The policy gave damage casters priority on the neck, on the argument that gearing damage cleared content faster. To the healers, it read differently: the people who kept everyone alive were structurally second in line for the best item they could ever get.

Nobody said much on the night. The resentment surfaced five weeks later, when Deliz — one of the guild's core healers and part of the Nittedal circle — quit the game entirely, naming the treatment of healers and their exclusion from best-in-slot rolls, with the Ragnaros neck as the concrete example. It was the guild's first fairness crisis, and its shape — effort versus optimisation, the meters versus the people who don't appear on them — returned in every loot fight that followed, from the tank-gear debates of spring to the benches of December.

milestones.title: Dejvid hands over the guild
milestones.titleHtml: Dejvid hands over the guild
milestones.blurb: Dejvid hands over Discord ownership; Artimis is guild leader in practice.
milestones.blurbHtml: Dejvid hands over Discord ownership; Artimis is guild leader in practice.
milestones.html:
Dejvid had founded Sleep with a complete joke of a rank ladder — Awake, Light Sleeper, Deep Sleeper, REM Sleeper, Dreamer — and a pitch about a helpful community. By early 2020 he was ready to step back, and the Discord ownership transfer on 1 February made official what the paperwork already showed: Artimis, the hunter officer with the spreadsheets, was running the guild. Dejvid stayed in the records as the founder; his best-documented later act was having promoted Shakey to priest class leader, a decision Artimis inherited along with everything else.

The transfer was formal on 1 February, but members were already treating it as done. On 30 January Thepaladin opened a tank-planning message with "since you took Dejvids place now," then briefed Artimis on the missing main tank. The title had followed the work before the paperwork caught up.

milestones.title: Deliz quits
milestones.blurb: Criticism of healers and the caster-first Choker policy; he leaves the game the same night.
milestones.blurbHtml: Criticism of healers and the caster-first Choker policy; he leaves the game the same night.
milestones.html: Deliz was Nittedal — one of the real-life friends the guild was built around — and a healer, which made his exit hurt twice. His complaint was structural, not personal: healers were excluded from best-in-slot rolls while damage dealers geared, with the Ragnaros Choker as the standing example. He quit the game the same night he said so. The question he left behind, what a raid owes the people who keep it alive but never top a meter, came back in every fairness crisis the guild ever had: the tank-gear fights of spring, the Rejuvenating Gem, and December's benches.

milestones.title: Blackwing Lair opens
milestones.blurb: Sleep enters on day one.
milestones.blurbHtml: Sleep enters on day one.
milestones.html: Sleep walked in on day one, twelve days into Artimis's formal leadership. The instance became the guild's home for half a year of Sundays — the place where the Dark Iron crafting projects, the gear-weight formulas and the Thunderfury bindings all earned their keep — and the site of its fastest conquest: the whole raid dead within ten days of the doors opening.

milestones.title: Nefarian falls
milestones.blurb: BWL 8/8 within ten days.
milestones.blurbHtml: BWL 8/8 within ten days.
milestones.html:
Ten days from the gates opening to the end boss dying — the fastest the guild ever moved through new content, and proof that the friendly community had quietly become a capable raid. The week also produced one of the archive's best recruitment stories: Artimis mailed a cloak to a stranger he had mistaken for someone else, invited him along to BWL anyway, and accidentally acquired Glory, the most loyal tank the guild would ever have.

The ten-day clear was not improvised. A guest healer from another guild sent Ragie a tank-switch video and offered outside coaching. Between raid nights the guild handed Ragie materials for several Dark Iron pieces so the tanks could survive Firemaw. Even the Onyxia-head buff was scheduled by the hour, until another player killed the NPC to move the reset.

milestones.title: Ragie disconnects on Onyxia
milestones.blurb: A routine Onyxia pull survives because the tank disconnects.
milestones.blurbHtml: A routine Onyxia pull survives because the tank disconnects.
milestones.html: The clip is titled as Ragie's disconnect pull and was uploaded on 12 March 2020. The video does not encode the pull date, and the available raid reports do not identify the correct run safely, so this milestone uses the publication date instead. The moment is early Sleep in miniature: a technical failure met by a room full of improvisation. Someone liked the mistake enough to preserve it.

milestones.title: The Nightfall experiment
milestones.blurb: Thepaladin secretly buys Nightfall; Sleep tests the legendary and rejects it on the numbers.
milestones.blurbHtml: Thepaladin secretly buys Nightfall; Sleep tests the legendary and rejects it on the numbers.
milestones.html:
The officers had agreed to fund one Nightfall, not two. Thepaladin made a private deal anyway, then confessed on 12 March that the axe had been sitting in his bags for a week. He asked for one Molten Core test rather than special treatment.

On the 15th the guild ran the experiment. Thepaladin measured nine percent debuff uptime overall and nineteen percent on Golemagg, while his own damage sat around 200 per second. Artimis compared that with the roughly 300 a regular warrior or rogue could bring and gave the verdict: "Does not seem worth it." Sleep had tested a legendary with a combat log and told its owner no.

milestones.title: First Rejuvenating Gem
milestones.blurb: Shakey wins the roll the day Fnats steps back.
milestones.blurbHtml: Shakey wins the roll the day Fnats steps back.
milestones.html: The full story of this night surfaced years later in a private thread. Fnats — druid, ex-mythic raider, one of the guild's two best healers — had spent about two months trying to get the gem's priority settled and eight days waiting for an answer about the healing-officer role, which had been advertised and previously held by Randy. Then Shakey, the priest leader Dejvid had appointed, won the first roll. That same evening Artimis offered Fnats the healing-officer role at last; Fnats took a break from the game instead, for exams and out of patience, with the line every guild leader eventually hears: "as guild leader, you unfortunately stand in the crossfire." His deeper point outlived the night — the people deciding loot for healers were people who would never play one.

milestones.title: Glory's first Binding
milestones.blurb: Both Garr and Baron Geddon die four times that night across split runs.
milestones.blurbHtml: Both Garr and Baron Geddon die four times that night across split runs.
milestones.html:
Four Garr and Baron Geddon kills in one night across split runs, and one of them finally dropped a Binding of the Windseeker for Glory. The same date marks the birth of the loot log itself: Artimis started the central spreadsheet that day with a plea that every class leader record every drop. Everything the loot pages on this site know traces back to that decision. The Binding also enrolled Glory in the guild's longest storyline — his Thunderfury completed in November 2020, weeks before December made the legendary feel like a parting gift.

Three weeks earlier Glory had forged Thepaladin's Sulfuron Hammer, another legendary project whose queue was being negotiated one player at a time.

milestones.title: The rogue loot revolt
milestones.blurb: Kodf's replacement awards himself tier pieces; the rogues demand their old system back.
milestones.blurbHtml: Kodf's replacement awards himself tier pieces; the rogues demand their old system back.
milestones.html:
Kodf left on 9 July after preparing Ntekapaz for a seventh rogue spot. The senior candidates declined his job, and Twx accepted it on the 13th after only three raids. His terms were explicit: seniority was out; parses, world buffs, spec, and consumables would decide loot.

Within two weeks Tsakimo had quit. Ntekapaz reported that Twx equipped two items without discussion and awarded himself the available tier pieces. Artimis checked the performance argument against the logs and found that the new leader had neither the best damage nor the best parses. His private conclusion was simpler: "I wish some Rogue that can do Kodf system would be interested in being class leader." By Dusk, Twx was gone too.

milestones.title: The baby announcement
milestones.blurb: Nefarian dies twice; Artimis tells the raid he is expecting a child and promotes Divinestorm on the spot.
milestones.blurbHtml: Nefarian dies twice; Artimis tells the raid he is expecting a child and promotes Divinestorm on the spot.
milestones.html:
The screenshots catch it all in the same minute: Nefarian dead for the second time that evening, the raid chat filling with congratulations, and the guild-system line recording that Artimis has made Divinestorm the new Guild Master. He told the raid he was going to be a father and gave the guild away in the same breath. Nereb, Pnats, Carmelia, Zados and Luivi answered in kind; Zados thanked the old leader and welcomed the new one in a single message. Nobody in the archive ever managed a cleaner exit.

The private version was less settled. Later that evening Artimis told a departing member that merger talks were advancing despite his own reservations, and that the decision now belonged to the officers who wanted it. The reply was a warning from experience: mergers make players quit. Twelve days later Sleep became Dusk.

The child arrived in the final days of December. By early January Artimis was declining outside raid invitations because the baby needed the time, closing the guest-raiding side story almost as soon as the guild story ended.

milestones.title: Sleep + Ninjas become Dusk
milestones.blurb: A new name from a poll, so neither guild absorbs the other.
milestones.blurbHtml: A new name from a poll, so neither guild absorbs the other.
milestones.html:
The name came from a poll precisely so that neither guild could claim the other had been swallowed — which is exactly what the Ninjas officers privately believed they were doing. Their channel from the merger weeks calls it "absorbing their guild" outright, and one scout who watched a Sleep raid doubted the merchandise could clear AQ. The Ninjas officers took a formal emoji vote on the 15th; the first raid as Dusk was planned within the week. Sleep's farewell post asked everyone to "make the move over to the Dusk discord with ease" — a server that still exists today under a different name.

The change had leaked in private long before the poll. On 23 July Artimis tried to persuade Tsakimo not to leave by promising that "big changes" might remove Twx as his class leader. Another departing member gave the merger its best warning: every merger he had seen made players quit. Dusk cleared C'Thun in five days, then spent September proving that success and stability were different things.

milestones.title: First Dusk AQ40
milestones.blurb: The preparation machine: resistance sets, rerolled professions, consumable pipelines.
milestones.blurbHtml: The preparation machine: resistance sets, rerolled professions, consumable pipelines.
milestones.html:
The preparation machine behind this night was the merged guild's first real product: nature-resistance sets planned in spreadsheets, professions rerolled on schedule, and a consumables pipeline that would soon be counting venom sacs in the hundreds. Four bosses died on the first evening. C'Thun followed within five days, answering the Ninjas scouts' doubts about "the quality to clear AQ" faster than anyone had a right to expect.

Tsakimo returned on this exact night after quitting Sleep over the July rogue loot system. His first request was access to the spreadsheet so he could record the drops. The merged guild's first raid therefore began with one of the old guild's casualties back at the bookkeeping.

The server move was still incomplete that afternoon. Exclusafk could not sign up because he lacked a role in the Dusk Discord, while the old Sleep server still carried a parallel signup. The new guild entered AQ before all its permissions had caught up.

milestones.title: The Ninjas bloc departs
milestones.blurb: Nearly the whole ex-Ninjas core raids its last Dusk night; the merger has failed.
milestones.blurbHtml: Nearly the whole ex-Ninjas core raids its last Dusk night; the merger has failed.
milestones.html: The morning began with Orish quitting live in the officer channel — "Leadership's going to run this guild into the ground, I'm out before it gets much worse" — the second ex-Ninjas officer gone in a week, after Aki's exit over the entrance-pull affair. By afternoon the structure itself had changed: Rockafella said the quiet part ("class leaders think they are officers"), and the officers split the chat in two within the hour. The same day's debate about publishing the officer logs — "we can just let people read the officer chat" against "how do we handle another Nayla situation?" — is the most honest conversation about transparency the guild ever had.

milestones.title: GM crisis
milestones.blurb: Yeat transfers guild master mid-conflict; Divinestorm manages it remotely.
milestones.blurbHtml: Yeat transfers guild master mid-conflict; Divinestorm manages it remotely.
milestones.html:
The strangest day in the record: Yeat, holding the in-game guild-master character, kicked Snjór. Henne said someone then reinvited Snjór and that he, or his alt, kicked her; Snjór's later account disputed the surrounding blame. Protest gquits followed. Divinestorm managed the crisis from a work trip, several people returned, and kick rights were restricted for good. Henne's terms for returning were the shortest in the archive: "Keep Snjór away from me and he can take the drama with him. And I'm good."

Artimis's same-day private summary was blunter than the public repair: "A lot of drama happening today in Dusk," followed by "drama between all the Ninja officers." Asked whether it came from outside the game, he answered yes. It does not resolve the underlying accusation, but it fixes how one officer understood the conflict while it was happening.

milestones.title: Thunderfury
milestones.blurb: Glory's second Binding drops; the legendary is announced the same evening.
milestones.blurbHtml: Glory's second Binding drops; the legendary is announced the same evening.
milestones.html:
Glory's second Binding closed a storyline that had run since March, and the guild announced the completed legendary the same evening. It was the raider-rank promise made physical: show up for a hundred raids, do the unglamorous work, and the guild forges you the most famous weapon in the game. Five weeks later the same guild benched him through every Four Horsemen pull. Both things are true, and the distance between them is the whole December story.

The queue had accumulated its own folklore by July. Three right-hand Bindings had dropped: one left with Kugel, one sat with Glory, and the other belonged to the current main-tank plan. Ragie was reserved the next Garr half, with Zhèna behind him for a future right half. One short-lived rogue leader claimed to own a Binding bought outside the guild, but the officers never verified it. Glory's completion was the opposite: every part of it sat in the shared record.

milestones.title: Nayla leaves
milestones.blurb: 113 logged sessions; felt unequal to the other tanks.
milestones.blurbHtml: 113 logged sessions; felt unequal to the other tanks.
milestones.html: The exit had three acts: the August discipline case that ended in "one final chance," the September telephone game over his tank spot, and a November departure with a flourish — messages to guildmates about their leader's "last desperate act of evilness," the details of which the archive still doesn't hold. Within two weeks he was raiding elsewhere and loudly himself on the realm Discord. A hundred and thirteen logged sessions deserve the honest summary: he gave the guild enormous amounts of his time, and cost it almost as much.

milestones.title: Dusk enters Naxxramas
milestones.blurb: Three bosses on the first night.
milestones.blurbHtml: Three bosses on the first night.
milestones.html: Noth, Anub'Rekhan and Grand Widow Faerlina fell on Dusk's first night in the citadel — but the run convinced the leadership the guild could not clear Naxxramas alone. The internal review afterwards was blunt, and within forty-eight hours the first conversation with Ascension had happened. The Faerlina kill video is the last recording of Dusk raiding as itself.

milestones.title: Joint raid with Ascension
milestones.blurb: Exactly 20 from each guild, picking the strongest players.
milestones.blurbHtml: Exactly 20 from each guild, picking the strongest players.
milestones.html: Six new bosses died on the first joint evening — Patchwerk, Grobbulus, Gluth, Thaddius, Heigan and Instructor Razuvious — vindicating the partnership overnight and hardening the roster math that had benched twenty people to make it possible. The kill videos from this night carry both guild names in their titles; eleven days later the titles just said Ascension.

milestones.title: Benched — a strike brews
milestones.blurb: Artimis organizes a protest over veterans losing seats; a 37-minute call resolves it the next day.
milestones.blurbHtml: Artimis organizes a protest over veterans losing seats; a 37-minute call resolves it the next day.
milestones.html:
The Four Horsemen wall — twelve wipes on the Sunday — sharpened everything: who tanked, who healed, and who watched from outside. On the Monday morning Artimis circulated a five-point proposal demanding raiders before members, whole-lockout spots, and collective bench decisions, while the officers held their own open reckoning about the same grievances in parallel. That evening the Horsemen died on the first pull; neither Artimis nor Glory, the two names at the center of the benching debate, was in the kill — though the private messages show Divinestorm pursuing Artimis all afternoon for a talk ("I know your points"), holding the call at 18:34, and Artimis offering to come once his evening walk ended; the raid filled and killed the Horsemen before he was back. The same night, Divinestorm invited him into the joint officer chat with Ascension. The video is the fight from Artimis's own vantage point in a later run.

The first-pull chest produced Corrupted Ashbringer for Randyfist. Artimis congratulated him by private message at 20:52, warning that the sword made its holder temporarily hated by the Argent Dawn. The strike letter's night ended with one of the game's most famous weapons.

At 21:34 Artimis told an outside raid leader that his guild had just killed the Four Horsemen. The offhand message independently fixes the kill to 14 December, after the argument and before the archive had time to turn it into a milestone.

milestones.title: Kel'Thuzad dies
milestones.blurb: Three wipes, then the last boss of vanilla. 43 names.
milestones.blurbHtml: Three wipes, then the last boss of vanilla. 43 names.
milestones.html: Sapphiron died at 19:53, Kel'Thuzad at 21:23 — Naxxramas cleared fourteen days after the first joint raid, the goal every December sacrifice had been aimed at. The full stream preserves all three attempts and the kill; the short cut is the celebration version. Within days, several of the people who had stayed for the clear left the game, exactly as they had said they would.

milestones.title: Glory's own Kel'Thuzad
milestones.blurb: Left out of the first kill, the guild's most-attended raider gets his — in the archive's final report.
milestones.blurbHtml: Left out of the first kill, the guild's most-attended raider gets his — in the archive's final report.
milestones.html: The last report in the whole archive contains its best ending. Glory — who left Dusk on the night it dissolved, having never been given a Four Horsemen pull — appears in an Ascension-era roster on 11 April 2021, and Kel'Thuzad dies. The guild's most-attended raider got the kill four months late, in the final raid the logs would ever record. History does not usually clean up after itself this well.

milestones.title: The Dusk list
milestones.blurb: Supplier posts a tribute video for every guildmate — the closest thing the guild ever made to its own memorial.
milestones.blurbHtml: Supplier posts a tribute video for every guildmate — the closest thing the guild ever made to its own memorial.
milestones.html:
With TBC weeks away and the old raid team scattered into new guilds, Supplier posted a list in the dying officer channel: one YouTube link per guildmate, a song or video chosen for each person. Fizzi was disappointed ("I was expecting funny gameplay videos"), Rakaiah demanded one and got it ("had to dig deep to find you"), and Teo was told his would have to be written from scratch. It reads today like the guild taking attendance one last time.
